male.name: The Challakere groundnut farmer
male.tagline: Rainfed Kuruba farmer who diversifies with sheep as the kaval grazing commons shrink.

household.who: Wife, works the farm and tends the sheep
Son, about 16, in government high school

dayInLife.text: Checks the two borewells that irrigate part of his groundnut and onion plots.
Moves his flock of eight to ten sheep out to graze on the remaining kaval commons.
Walks his fields checking for pest damage.
He and his wife register for MGNREGA work, which supplements rather than replaces farm income.
Sells sheep as a buffer, since groundnut and onion prices are volatile.

topics.label: Daily Life & Work
topics.headline: Diversifying across crops and sheep to survive drought and price swings
points: Groundnut and onion rotate with ragi on about three rainfed acres; sheep act as a buffer in bad years.
One of his two borewells failed two years ago when the water table dropped further.
A bumper crop can crash onion prices from Rs 40-50 a kilogram to Rs 5-10 within weeks.

stat.label: Monthly household income, averaged over good and bad seasons, before loan repayments

topics.label: Family & Household
topics.headline: Women's labour is central, but credit and land sit with men
points: His wife works alongside him and manages the sheep, on top of unpaid domestic labour and childcare.
He handles loan and land transactions; day-to-day decisions are made jointly with his wife.
He hopes his son finishes school; he is less certain about his daughter's path beyond secondary school.

stat.label: Female vs male literacy, Chitradurga district, 2011 Census

topics.label: Education & Schooling
topics.headline: No secondary school within walking distance, and a daughter nearing Class 9
points: His son commutes several kilometres to a government high school in Challakere town by bicycle or shared transport.
His daughter must move to the same distant high school at Class 9; no girls' secondary school is nearer.
He knows the Kasturba Gandhi Balika Vidyalaya residential scheme and sees it as a fallback.

stat.label: Karnataka dropout rate in classes 9-10, UDISE+ 2023-24

topics.label: Health & Wellbeing
topics.headline: Heat, pesticides and debt anxiety, with serious care far away
points: He sprays pesticide with minimal protection and has had skin irritation and headaches, without a formal diagnosis.
Routine illness goes to a primary health centre nearby; serious cases mean travelling to Chitradurga town.
His wife has chronic back and joint pain that she manages without regular medical attention.

stat.label: Karnataka farmer suicides, April 2023-July 2024, mostly drought and debt-linked

topics.label: Community & Belief
topics.headline: Identity shaped by the kaval grazing commons and their loss
points: He identifies with the Kuruba community, traditionally dependent on the Amrita Mahal Kaval commons for grazing.
He is Hindu and attends his village deity's festivals as markers of the farming and social calendar.
Caste associations and village elders' councils informally settle disputes over land, grazing rights and marriage.

stat.label: Kaval grazing land diverted since 2009-2010 for the Challakere science city

topics.label: Civic Life & Government
topics.headline: Slow compensation and shrinking MGNREGA work shape his view of the state
points: He has filed drought-relief claims and calls the process slow and paperwork-heavy.
His wife and daughter benefit from the Shakti scheme's free bus travel for women.
He attends gram sabha meetings to raise the kaval dispute, borewell electricity connections and the hamlet road.

stat.label: Farmer suicides deemed eligible for Rs 5 lakh compensation, April 2023-July 2024

topics.label: Worldview & Concerns
topics.headline: Water first, then compensation, grazing land and local jobs
points: His most immediate worry is water: one borewell failure can wipe out a season's investment overnight.
He is proud of keeping the household afloat and of his son staying in school this long.
The science city took land but, in his community's eyes, has employed relatively few local people.

stat.label: Karnataka taluks declared disaster-affected in the 2023 drought

schoolPressures.label: Distance
schoolPressures.detail: No functioning secondary school within walking distance; the daily commute to Challakere town is several kilometres.

schoolPressures.label: Harvest labour
schoolPressures.detail: Farm and grazing work during the groundnut harvest and lambing season pulls children away.

schoolPressures.label: Lost grazing land
schoolPressures.detail: Kaval diversion changed herding routines, pulling boys who help move livestock away from regular schooling.

schoolPressures.label: Drought wage work
schoolPressures.detail: In bad years a teenager may do short stretches of daily-wage work while staying on school rolls.

female.name: The Chintamani silkworm rearer
female.tagline: Rears silkworms and works daily wages, running the household alone while her husband migrates.

household.who: Husband, migrates seasonally for brick-kiln and construction work

dayInLife.text: Cuts and carries mulberry leaves to feed the silkworms.
Feeds worms several times a day, cleans trays and manages shed temperature and humidity by hand.
Takes daily wage work transplanting or harvesting in tomato and grape fields, with no guaranteed work.
Her husband travels to brick kilns or construction sites, leaving her to run everything.
Cooking, water collection and childcare come on top of both kinds of paid work.

topics.label: Daily Life & Work
topics.headline: Two kinds of labour that rarely let up
points: She rears silkworms on a rented quarter-acre of mulberry and takes daily wage work in nearby fields.
Women dominate cocoon harvesting, worm-mounting, leaf-feeding and rearing, while men usually market the cocoons.
A poor rearing cycle, silkworm disease or a market dip can wipe out weeks of unpaid labour.

stat.label: Monthly household income, averaged across rearing cycles, wage days and migration earnings

topics.label: Family & Household
topics.headline: She runs the household largely alone while her husband is away
points: She studied only to about Class 6 before leaving to help her mother with younger siblings.
During her husband's absences she decides on children's schooling, health spending and the daily budget.
She sometimes takes her daughter along to cut mulberry leaves and feed silkworms in busy rearing cycles.

stat.label: Women per 1,000 men, Chikkaballapur district, 2011 Census

topics.label: Education & Schooling
topics.headline: Her daughter's Class 9 decision is genuinely undecided
points: Her son commutes daily to a government high school in Chintamani town; her daughter finished Class 8.
The nearest school with Classes 9 and 10 is several kilometres away, and parents weigh safety heavily.
A Kasturba Gandhi Balika Vidyalaya hostel seat is one of the few realistic ways her daughter could continue.

stat.label: Karnataka girls' dropout rate in 2023-24, falling to 13.9% by 2025-26

topics.label: Health & Wellbeing
topics.headline: Fluoride in groundwater, aching backs and a distant referral hospital
points: Studies find fluoride in the district's groundwater above safe limits; she notes mottled teeth among some village children.
Sericulture work is linked to back and joint pain, skin irritation and eye strain; she treats hers unaided.
Anything serious means R.L. Jalappa Hospital in Tamaka, Kolar, a journey of an hour or more.

stat.label: Tested groundwater samples in Chikkaballapur taluk over fluoride limits, 2024 study

topics.label: Community & Belief
topics.headline: A bilingual border community held together by women's networks
points: Kannada, Telugu and, in the town's older core, Urdu are all spoken in Chintamani taluk.
She is Hindu and attends the village temple's annual festival; neighbouring silkworm-rearing women are her closest ties.
She is wary of outsiders assuming everyone speaks only Kannada or that sericulture is easy cottage labour.

topics.label: Civic Life & Government
topics.headline: Sericulture services and free bus rides, but opaque hostel seats
points: She is registered with the district sericulture network of cocoon markets and grainage centres, including one in Chintamani.
The Shakti scheme gives her free bus travel to the bank, taluk office or a larger cocoon market.
She asked about Kasturba Gandhi Balika Vidyalaya seats and found eligibility opaque and dependent on teachers' contacts.

stat.label: Free rides recorded statewide under Shakti since June 2023

topics.label: Worldview & Concerns
topics.headline: Unpredictable cocoon prices and wage days, with small failures adding up
points: Her top worry is two unpredictable incomes at once: cocoon prices and wage-labour availability.
She would likely demand tested piped water and steadier cocoon procurement prices.
She takes pride in keeping her son in school and managing the household alone while her husband is away.

schoolPressures.label: Distance & safety
schoolPressures.detail: The nearest Class 9-10 school is several kilometres away, and parents weigh the commute and daughters' safety heavily.

schoolPressures.label: Rearing labour
schoolPressures.detail: Time-bound leaf-feeding and rearing work often falls to daughters, especially when the father is away.

schoolPressures.label: Father's migration
schoolPressures.detail: Seasonal brick-kiln and construction work leaves no one to share the load and disrupts children's attendance.

schoolPressures.label: Hostel seat uncertainty
schoolPressures.detail: Continuing depends on whether a KGBV or similar hostel seat becomes available and how cocoon cycles pay.
